newsitem.title: UK: BT wins 700 million pound UK defence contract.
newsitem.headline: BT wins 700 million pound UK defence contract.

text.p: The British government said on Wednesday it had decided to award a 10-year contract to provide a new defence fixed telecommunications system to a consortium led by British Telecommunications Plc.

Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said in a written parliamentary answer that the contract would be worth 700 million pounds ($1.15 billion). Senior defence ministry officials later said the overall value of the contract would be closer to one billion pounds over its 10-year life once user tariffs were taken into account.
Other members of the winning consortium include U.S. company Lockheed Martin and British firm GEC-Marconi, a unit of the General Electric Co Plc.
Officials said the new contract was expected to cut the Ministry of Defence's telephone bill by around 15 percent to about 85 million pounds a year, saving it some 150 million pounds over 10 years.
